feasible.reason: The headline half of FI-05 — charge the PIN budget on every sentinel/CFI/receipt trip and wipe on a re-entrant fault — does not deliver the bound it claims and re-introduces a design two independent reviewers already rejected on this repo. (1) FACTUAL ERROR in the mechanism: `pin_attempts_bump` charges ONLY MCU page 124. `reconcile_pin_attempts` (secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1661-1710) wipes when `se_count > mcu` and tolerates an MCU lead; it never advances E120 or the SE050 UserID. So the proposal charges the one counter that is not silicon-backed and leaves the extraction-resistant backstop (E120, SE050 UserID) untouched — it is not a "three-way" charge. (2) BYPASS / REDUNDANCY against the stated threat: every post-unlock FI site the proposal names (c10_sign_verified ct_eq, CfiCounter, sign-dispatch defaults, fw_update) is reachable only by an adversary who can unlock. A successful `gated_unlock` resets page 124 to 0 (nsc/mod.rs:1593, 1714), so a PIN-holding adversary re-unlocks after each charged trip and is never bounded; a PIN-less thief can only reach those sites inside the 120 s theft window, where the existing `zeroize_sensitive_state` relock (crypto.rs:373-391) already ends the campaign after ONE trip because re-entry needs the PIN. Pre-unlock, `gated_unlock` already precharges page 124 before every SE call (nsc/mod.rs:1473), so wrong-PIN glitch trials are not free today; the remaining uncharged pre-unlock sites (pointer validation, IS_UNLOCKED, reconcile, first-boot) hold no secrets on a locked device. Net: part (1) bounds nothing that is not already bounded. (3) IT CONVERTS BENIGN/NS-TRIGGERABLE EVENTS INTO WALLET DESTRUCTION: the sink routes SCP03/CCM receipt failures and `read_volatile_voted` CounterUnstable through charge-then-wipe, but silicon already shows those fire with no attacker (#715: 10 attempts consumed after a CORRECT PIN; #692: persistent SE fault burns the whole budget; #109: transport glitch after a successful verify charges an attempt). The `in_progress ⇒ immediate wipe` rule is worse: `wait_random_loop`'s halt is reachable from ISR context (the production-forced consumption-mask SysTick reseed, #835 C1) and from compromised NS firmware preempting a secure call into `nsc_is_unlocked` (#835 H5), so a fault "reported while one is being handled" is a scheduling event, not a second glitch — compromised NS gets a wipe-the-user's-wallet primitive. #835 (OPEN, critical) is precisely the adjudication of the earlier #833/#834 halt sink that burned page 124 on sentinel trips: both reviewers concluded "a transient event must not be able to spend a user's PIN attempts, let alone all ten" and rated the sink net-negative. FI-05 re-proposes that policy with a wider trigger set and adds an SE wipe, without first closing C1/C2/H5. (4) Cost/priority is misallocated: the genuinely valuable, cheap item is part (2) (H4 — zeroize + mask IRQs before `halt_on_glitch`), which is an S-cost fix with no policy decision; bundling it under a P1 "charge and wipe" banner delays it behind an owner decision the repo has already declined once.
feasible.corrections: Split FI-05. KEEP as a separate S-cost P1 item: (a) `halt_on_glitch` must zeroize before parking — but it lives in `pqsigner-fi` (pure-logic crate, no access to `nsc::zeroize_sensitive_state`) and is shared with the FSBL, so it needs a registered `extern`/callback hook (same pattern as the `pqsigner_sha256_*` hooks) that the secure world binds to `zeroize_sensitive_state` + `cpsid i` and the FSBL leaves bare; run it on a fresh stack if the panic-handler convention is adopted; TAMP BKERASE of the BHK regs is acceptable only because page 126 holds the DHUK-wrapped BHK for re-load on reboot (verify that re-load path exists before adding BKERASE, otherwise it is a wipe, not a halt-zeroize); it does NOT violate #484 (that rule is about attacker-owned display/SPI, not SRAM/TAMP). (b) Sparse-random phase words for the fw_update/first-boot/sign-dispatch state machines (part 3) — fine as written, no policy content. DROP or REWRITE part (1): charging page 124 is MCU-only (E120/UserID are advanced only by SE-side wrong-PIN verifies; reconciliation never advances them) and is reset by every correct unlock, so it bounds no adversary the relock does not already bound. If the owner still wants an escalation ladder, restrict it to CONFIRMED-fault sites where benign causes are provably excluded (the double-compute `ct_eq` mismatch, CfiCounter mismatch, sentinel value that is neither OK nor FAIL) and make the escalation a durable `page-125` "fault-count" that is NOT reset by a correct PIN and triggers admin wipe at N — that is the only form that survives the re-unlock bypass; never include SCP03/CCM receipt failures, CounterUnstable, or `wait_random_loop` halts (benign on silicon per #715/#692/#109, ISR/NS-reachable per #835 C1/H5). Do not implement any `in_progress ⇒ wipe` rule until #835 C1, C2 and H5 are closed, and reject re-entry from exception context explicitly (Trezor's handle_fault is single-threaded storage code; ours would be hit from SysTick). Fix the "vendor_precedent" framing: Trezor charges the PIN counter only inside storage's own PIN-check fault handler, not on every sentinel trip firmware-wide. Re-tag cost: part (2)+(3) = S; part (1) = M plus an owner decision that #835 already argues against.

vendor-claim.reason: The vendor_precedent is accurate in substance: Trezor ships exactly the handle_fault pattern (storage/storage.c:1815-1844: static secbool in_progress; re-entrant fault ⇒ storage_wipe; otherwise pin_get_fails → storage_pin_fails_increase → re-read and require ctr+1 → __fatal_error), the bootloader WF_ERROR_FATAL/default ⇒ secret_bhk_regenerate + erase_storage + backup_ram_erase_protected (core/embed/projects/bootloader/main.c:677-690), and the fresh-stack + RAM-fill halt/reboot (bootutils.c:103-137 halt_device_phase_2/halt_device, :140-198 reboot_with_args_phase_2) with BKERASE+SRAM2 erase. The sparse-random phase-word idea is also Trezor precedent (workflow_common.h:23-33, WF_ERROR_FATAL=0 with `default:` fallthrough; secbool sectrue=0xAAAAAAAA at rtl/secbool.h:25-26). No vendor demonstrably ships something stronger, so novelty='parity' stands. The repo_evidence lines are all confirmed as cited. Corrections are needed on five points (below), none of which overturns the precedent or novelty claim.
vendor-claim.corrections: (1) Citation fix: BKERASE is NOT in bootutils.c:103-199. It lives in call_with_new_stack, core/embed/sys/startup/stm32/sysutils.c:31-79 (CPSID F; disable MPU; on STM32U5 with clear_bkpregs: clear RCC SAESEN then TAMP->CR2 |= BKERASE; new MSP/MSPLIM; clear registers). bootutils.c:137 and :198 call it with clear_bkpregs=true. halt_device exists only under RSOD_INFINITE_LOOP (model headers T2T1/T2B1/T3T1/T3B1/T3T2); battery models reboot instead (bootutils.c:36-41 #error), but the reboot path also RAM-fills + BKERASEs, so the secrets-cleared property holds either way. (2) Scope of Trezor's charge-on-fault is narrower than the proposal: handle_fault is used only inside storage.c (26 sites, e.g. :214,:377,:1219,:1429 — loop-completion, tag, version, auth-tag checks) and increments only the MCU norcow PIN-fail counter (pinlogs_*; the Optiga counter advances only inside optiga_pin_verify, storage.c:787-844). Every other Trezor fault check uses ensure() (rtl/error_handling.h:144-149) → __fatal_error → system_exit_fatal_ex → RSOD → halt/reboot with RAM clear, with NO attempt charge. So 'charge the PIN budget on every sentinel/CFI/receipt trip' is broader than Trezor; Trezor's shipped policy is: storage-integrity faults charge, everything else halt+wipe-RAM. (3) The Donjon Tangem source does not support 'charge on fault' as a recommendation — it documents how a post-detection persistent fault counter (inferred, ~256 events ⇒ permanent brick) was defeated by power-tearing on the flash-write signature ('unlimited retries'), and recommends redundant checks, Hamming-distant booleans and input validation instead. Trezor's handle_fault increments AFTER detection (storage.c:1831-1842) and thus has the same tearing window. The correct precedent shape is the PRECHARGE: Trezor storage.c:1210-1221 (increase before PIN check, verify ctr+1) and PQSigner's own gated_unlock (secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1473 pin_attempts_bump before se.unlock, verified via check_true_into_sentinel). A sink that charges after the trip should be stated as tearable, or the charge must be precharged at the authorization site. (4) 'which also advances E120/UserID on the next unlock by construction of the directional reconciliation' is unsupported by the code: pin_attempts_bump charges page 124 only; reconcile_pin_attempts (secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1636-1700) treats an MCU lead as benign (power-cut/flaky-I2C) and never catches E120/UserID up; the SE counters advance only on an actual SE wrong-PIN verify. The sink as proposed is a one-way MCU-page-124 charge, not a three-way charge; CLAUDE.md invariant #2 already forbids calling this three-way. (5) 'every primitive already exists' is partly false: TAMP BKERASE does not exist in PQSigner (grep BKERASE secure/src → none; secure/src/hw/tamp.rs:304 notes no backup-SRAM data); BHK regs are only read (secure/src/hw/saes.rs:541-559). What does exist: page-125 wipe flag (secure/src/hw/flash.rs:675-686), admin wipe (secure/src/dual_se.rs:689), zeroize_sensitive_state (secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1729-1747), panic handler zeroizes first (secure/src/main.rs:4712-4713). (6) '#835 H4 ... fixed only on perf/flash-opt-level-z' is inaccurate: that branch still carries the bare halt_on_glitch (git show perf/flash-opt-level-z:pqsigner-fi/src/lib.rs lines 263-274, callers at 144/153); commit 7594e606 removed the halt-sink CALLERS ('the HALT goes'), it did not make the halt zeroize. H4 is unfixed as a halt-zeroize anywhere. (7) Policy collision not named in risks: #835 (OPEN) finding C3, by both independent reviewers, states 'A transient TRNG event must not be able to spend a user's PIN attempts' — charging page 124 on every sentinel trip (there are ~800 wait_random/check_true* sites, #835 H5) reproduces exactly the rejected C3 behaviour unless the sink is restricted to verdict-inconsistency sites (ct_eq mismatch, CFI mismatch, receipt MAC failure) and excludes RNG-unavailable/SE-unreachable/pointer-validation classes. Trezor's storage-only scoping (point 2) is the precedent for that restriction. (8) Other vendors: Ledger publishes only that its SE has light/voltage/temperature detectors and 'appropriate security reactions' (ledger.com academy pages); its post-detection policy is undocumented, so no Ledger precedent can be cited either way. Tangem (per Donjon) is a shipped-product precedent for fault ⇒ persistent counter ⇒ permanent brick, with the tearing caveat. No public Coldcard Mk4 / BitBox02 fault-response policy was found (Coinkite's Donjon response discusses triple-chip key split, not fault escalation).
